ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), SC 2000, c. 17, as amended, and Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; FINTRAC Guidance 6 and 2 on beneficial ownership and politically exposed persons; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c. C-46, ss. 83.05 (terrorist entity list) and 462.31 (laundering proceeds); Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c. 17; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2011, c. 10; United Nations Act, SC 1991, c. 24; Income Tax Act, RSC 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.), ss. 233.2 and 233.3. Provincial: Alberta Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c. P-3 (registration and declaration of limited partnerships); Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c. B-9 (name, registered office and records rules applicable to any corporate general partner); Beneficial Ownership Transparency Act, SC 2024, c. 19 (federal CBCA public beneficial-ownership registry framework, not yet extended to Alberta limited partnerships).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory baseline screening of every general partner, limited partner and any individual satisfying the 25% beneficial-ownership threshold against: (i) OFAC SDN List including sub-entities; (ii) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) Global Affairs Canada autonomous sanctions schedules under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act; (iv) Criminal Code s. 83.05 terrorist entity list; (v) FINTRAC/PCMLTFA foreign and domestic politically exposed person (PEP) definitions; (vi) INTERPOL Red Notices and adverse-media / enforcement-action databases (FINTRAC, OSFI, RCMP, ASIC, SEC); and (vii) Stripe and PayPal merchant underwriting prohibited-business and sanctioned-country matrices, given target payment rails of Kickstarter-Stripe and PayPal. The business is assessed as Low_Risk_Standard, not an MSB, and requires no FINTRAC registration; however, the LP must assemble and retain a FINTRAC-compliant KYC file with source-of-funds evidence for each capital contribution and re-screen principals on a change-of-control event.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance_note: Canada acceded to the Hague Apostille Convention effective 11 January 2024; so-called 'double legalization' for documents originating in non-Hague states follows Global Affairs Canada consular legalization policy.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry - CORES (Corporate Online Registration Extranet System), operated by Service Alberta, filing through licensed Alberta Registry Agents at https://www.alberta.ca/corporate-registry; federal trademark-conflict scanning via the NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) portal administered by Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Registered LP names must be expressed in Latin-script English (or French where federally required); non-Latin scripts (Cyrillic, CJK, runic and other vernacular brand marks) must be transliterated to Latin characters in the formal name, with the vernacular version permitted only as an unregistered trading/style name. The name must be distinguishable from existing Alberta and extra-provincial names, must satisfy the registrability conditions of the Alberta Partnership Act and, where the general partner is a corporation, ABCA s. 12, and must carry the mandatory 'Limited Partnership' or accepted 'L.P.'/'LP' designation. Purely descriptive or generic gaming terms such as 'Polyhedral' or 'Dice' generally fail distinctiveness review; a coined distinctive mark (e.g., combining a fanciful term with 'D20' or a house brand) is recommended and should be pre-cleared for Trade-marks Act s. 9 protected marks and common-law goodwill conflicts.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Royal / Crown / Government / Canada / Alberta (false Crown or governmental association)
Olympic / Commonwealth / RCMP / Royal Canadian Mounted Police
Saint / Church / Christian / Charitable (requires consent or charitable status)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant (1) obtains written reasons from the Alberta Registrar or the Registry Agent refusal notice; (2) files a new Name Search Report with a distinctly coined name, restarting a fresh 90-day reservation window; (3) where the refusal is based on likelihood of confusion, submits a comparative confusion memorandum citing Trade-marks Act ss. 12 and 16 factors and evidence of prior or concurrent use; (4) files an administrative appeal with the Registrar within 30 days of the refusal under the Alberta Partnership Act / ABCA administration procedures; (5) if the Registrar's decision is patently unreasonable, applies for judicial review to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under the Administrative Procedures and Jurisdiction Act, RSA 2000, c. A-3; and (6) as a fallback, reserves a different name promptly to avoid holding up the Stage-2 registration. The 90-day reservation cannot be statutorily elongated; refiling and a new fee restart the window, and priority is lost on expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A licensed Alberta registered agent's virtual office that provides a physical street address in Alberta is acceptable as the LP's address for service in the Partnership Act declaration, provided no P.O. Box is used and the agent is authorized to accept service of process. However, the registered office cannot be a bare mail-forwarding box for the actual trade: the epoxy-resin dice casting operation requires a real premises satisfying municipal zoning, fire safety and WHMIS / Hazardous Products Act handling rules, whether a home-based craft studio or a light-industrial workshop. Kickstarter and PayPal merchant underwriting will also require a verifiable physical operating address distinct from the agent address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for registry and income-tax purposes: approx. 3-5% annual probability of an unannounced CRA audit field visit or corporate-registry premises check for a non-licensed, low-risk goods LP. Municipal by-law and fire-safety inspection probability rises to approx. 15-20% per year if epoxy resin and liquid-core materials are handled in a residential zone, on account of chemical storage and ventilation requirements. No FINTRAC on-site AML examination applies unless the entity later becomes an MSB or payment-services intermediary.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Alberta Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c P-3, including sections 51-62 governing limited partnerships, registration, limited partner status, and partnership particulars.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, administered by Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction through authorized registry agents.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Limited Partnership, filed in the prescribed Alberta Corporate Registry form, together with the required partnership name and registered-office particulars.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital or mandatory escrow account applies to an Alberta limited partnership. The partnership agreement should specify each partner's committed contribution, timing, withdrawal restrictions, allocation of profits and losses, and liability limitations. A general partner must be appointed and must assume unlimited partnership liability unless separately structured through a corporate general partner.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the General Partner approve formation and registration of the Alberta limited partnership under the Partnership Act; approve the partnership name, registered office, and records address; authorize execution and filing of the Declaration of Limited Partnership and partnership agreement; approve the stated capital commitments and contributions of the partners. Where the General Partner is a corporation, its board authorizes the corporation’s subscription for its agreed partnership interest and appoints the President, Secretary, and Treasurer as authorized officers. Any officer may execute registry, banking, tax, licensing, and commercial documents and take all actions necessary to implement these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm Partnership Structure and Name Availability
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry through an authorized Alberta registry agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select the general partner and limited partner or partners, define their contributions and commercial roles, and obtain an Alberta business name search or NUANS report if a non-numbered name is proposed. Confirm that the name is not misleading, confusingly similar, prohibited, or inconsistent with Alberta naming rules. Reserve the name where appropriate before filing.
required_dossiers: Business name search or NUANS report, if required
Identity and address information for each partner
Corporate certificates and authorizations for any corporate partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit an amended name or use a numbered limited partnership. If the registry identifies an information deficiency, obtain the written query, correct the name or particulars, and resubmit through the registry agent within the permitted correction period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private execution process; filing is completed through an Alberta Corporate Registry agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and execute a written limited partnership agreement covering the general partner's authority, limited partner contribution obligations, distributions, tax allocations, admission and withdrawal, transfer restrictions, indemnities, dissolution, dispute resolution, records, and authority to operate the dice manufacturing and online sales business. Notarization is not ordinarily required for Canadian signatories, but foreign execution documents should be legalized or apostilled where requested by the registry agent or financial institution.
required_dossiers: Corporate authorizing resolutions for corporate partners
Beneficial ownership and control information for financial institutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct execution defects, obtain missing corporate approvals, and re-execute inconsistent pages. If a foreign document is questioned, provide a certified English translation and applicable notarization, legalization, or apostille.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the Declaration of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry online services or an authorized registry agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the prescribed Declaration of Limited Partnership with the approved name, registered office, records address, general partner details, and other mandatory particulars. Pay the applicable Alberta-dollar registry and service-agent charges; Alberta does not impose a filing fee denominated in United States dollars. Obtain the Certificate of Registration and registry profile immediately after acceptance.
required_dossiers: Approved or reserved partnership name evidence
Limited partner details where required by the filing form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to a registry query through the filing agent, correct rejected particulars, replace defective name evidence, and resubmit the declaration. Preserve the rejection notice and final Certificate of Registration in the statutory records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establish Statutory Records and Governance Controls
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internal partnership records function; Alberta Corporate Registry for subsequent registered changes
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Maintain the Certificate of Registration, declaration, partnership agreement, partner contribution ledger, resolutions, accounting records, tax elections, contracts, and beneficial ownership information. Adopt signing authorities and conflict-of-interest controls. Record amendments to the general partner, registered office, name, or other registrable particulars and file required changes promptly.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a registered particular changes without filing, prepare the prescribed amendment immediately and obtain legal advice on any limitation-of-liability or third-party reliance consequences. Correct internal records and notify banks, payment processors, insurers, and counterparties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Tax, Banking, and Commercial Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency Business Registration Online; Alberta Treasury Board and Finance; financial institution or regulated payment provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a CRA Business Number for the partnership and register for GST/HST when required or voluntarily elected. Assess payroll, import/export, corporate income tax filing obligations of the partners, and provincial tax accounts. Open a partnership bank account using the registration certificate, agreement, resolutions, identification, and beneficial ownership information. Complete merchant onboarding for Stripe, Kickstarter, and PayPal using consistent legal-name and ownership data.
required_dossiers: Payroll registration information, if employees are hired
Partner tax residency and beneficial ownership information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to CRA or financial-provider verification requests with certified formation documents, tax-residency evidence, ownership charts, and source-of-funds records. Correct inconsistent names, addresses, or control data before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Local Premises and Workplace Approvals
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Relevant Alberta municipality, municipal planning and development department, building safety authority, fire authority, and Alberta Occupational Health and Safety authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before occupying or modifying a workshop, confirm zoning approval for light manufacturing, storage, retail, and home-based activity where relevant. Obtain development, building, electrical, gas, occupancy, and fire approvals applicable to the premises. Implement Alberta OHS controls for epoxy resins, curing agents, pigments, solvents, dust, ventilation, personal protective equipment, storage, spill response, and worker training.
required_dossiers: Chemical inventory and safety data sheets
OHS hazard assessment and safe-work procedures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an authority identifies an unsafe or non-conforming condition, suspend the affected activity, obtain the inspection report, complete corrective construction or safety measures, and request reinspection or permit amendment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No general Alberta industrial licensing board is ordinarily applicable to small-scale handmade epoxy-resin dice manufacturing. Relevant authorities are Alberta Corporate Registry, the applicable municipal planning and licensing department, Alberta Environment and Protected Areas, Alberta Occupational Health and Safety, and the local fire authority.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general provincial manufacturing licence is ordinarily required. A municipal business licence, development approval, occupancy permit, building permit, and fire inspection or clearance may be required depending on the municipality, premises, equipment, and scale of operations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally exempt from a full Environmental Impact Assessment for a small workshop, subject to site-specific screening. An Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act approval, registration, release reporting, waste authorization, or municipal sewer authorization may be required if operations create regulated releases, hazardous waste, significant emissions, or industrial wastewater.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Do not discharge uncured resin, hardener, pigments, solvents, or contaminated wash water to drains, soil, or stormwater. Control VOCs through closed containers, local exhaust ventilation, approved storage, and compliant waste handling. Classify and manage chemical and resin waste under Alberta requirements and municipal rules; obtain applicable approval before any regulated release. Maintain spill prevention, manifests or disposal records where required, and comply with municipal sewer acceptance limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain applicable municipal building, occupancy, electrical, ventilation, and fire approvals before operation. Maintain unobstructed exits, extinguishers, emergency lighting where required, chemical segregation, spill kits, and documented emergency procedures. Conduct structural and electrical inspections for shelving, curing equipment, compressed containers, and workshop loads. Complete Alberta OHS hazard assessments, worker training, WHMIS compliance, respiratory and skin-exposure controls, PPE selection, incident reporting, and workplace inspections.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — official online portal: My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/account-information-payment-information/overview-my-business-account.html)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Alberta Limited Partnership (LP) is not itself taxed as a separate income tax person, but it must obtain a Business Number (BN) from the CRA for GST/HST, payroll, and other program accounts where applicable. Procedure: (1) Confirm whether the LP is required to register for GST/HST by applying the small-supplier threshold test (see indirect taxation rules); (2) If registration is required, complete, either online via Business Registration Online (BRO) or by paper form RC1 'Request for a Business Number', and submit to the CRA; (3) Provide a certified copy of the LP’s registration certificate or partnership agreement from Alberta (or the home jurisdiction for extra-provincial registration), plus identification and Canadian/foreign addresses for the general partner(s) and each partner; (4) If the LP has no physical presence in Canada, designate a resident agent or use a non-resident registration pathway; (5) The CRA will issue a 9-digit BN and a GST/HST program account (ending in 'RT') as applicable; (6) Non-resident partners are subject to Canadian Part XIII withholding tax on paid/credited partnership amounts, reported via CRA Form NR4, and should apply for a non-resident withholding tax account; (7) Ensure the LP files any applicable annual information return (e.g., T5013 Partnership Information Return, even where tax-exempt, to report allocation of income to partners).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canadian law does not provide a 'check-the-box' entity classification election; an Alberta LP is statutorily flow-through for income tax. Permitted elections include: (a) a partnership fiscal period election under subsection 249.1(7) of the Income Tax Act (Canada); (b) GST/HST elections under sections 22 and 177 of the Excise Tax Act, such as the 'partner’s share' method for capital property; (c) an election to provide a non-resident partner with a waiver or reduction of Part XIII withholding under the Canada-United States Tax Treaty, where applicable; (d) for hybrid mismatch arrangements, Canada’s income tax rules (e.g., ITA s. 18.2, s. 18.4) impose designated-filing consequences but do not involve voluntary elections. The LP may also elect registration as a small supplier or to register voluntarily for GST/HST under section 240(1) of the ETA.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (Goods and Services Tax) / HST (Harmonized Sales Tax) — in Alberta only the federal 5% GST applies; there is no provincial sales tax or HST in AB.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — a person (including a non-resident partnership carrying on business in Canada) becomes a mandatory GST/HST registrant once its total taxable supplies in Canada exceed CAD 30,000 in a given calendar quarter or over the immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters, unless the supplies are zero-rated. Non-resident persons soliciting orders in Canada via a website, catalogue, or other telemarketing and delivering goods by mail or courier are also required to register once the CAD 30,000 threshold is exceeded, and may be permitted or required to use the simplified non-resident GST/HST registration and filing regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or government pre-approval of invoices. However, GST/HST tax invoices must meet prescribed content requirements under CRA regulations when the consideration is CAD 30 or more, including supplier name/BN, recipient name, date, description, and GST/HST rate and amount. Registered suppliers may issue electronic tax invoices without prior authorization, but must produce readable paper copies upon CRA request. GST/HST returns must be filed electronically (GST/HST NETFILE) in many cases, and the CRA requires XML/API-based integration for bulk filing or third-party software submissions through its gateway; businesses must retain electronic records and will be subject to CRA electronic audit access under the Income Tax Act and Excise Tax Act. No 'national clearance center' exists for export invoices; export documentation is verified during CRA audits and through customs export filings with the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of goods and services exported from Canada are generally zero-rated under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act. For goods: the supplier must be registered and the goods must be exported 'directly or indirectly' by the supplier, the recipient, or an agent of either, normally within 60 days after the sale; the supplier must maintain documentary evidence of exportation, such as a fully completed customs export declaration accepted by CBSA, a bill of lading or waybill showing a Canadian point of origin and a foreign destination, and proof that the non-resident customer wired payment in foreign currency. For services (including design/production services incidental to the manufacture of tabletop dice), zero-rating applies when the supply is made to a non-resident person, the supply is not in connection with real estate in Canada, and the recipient is outside Canada at the time of the supply; if the service is rendered to a person in Canada before export, it may be taxable. A GST/HST registered LP can claim input tax credits (ITCs) on inputs used to produce the zero-rated export supplies, and any GST/HST paid on inputs will be available for refund or offset against tax due. Substantiation must be retained in either paper or electronic form and made available to the CRA upon audit.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA may conduct targeted audits of zero-rating claims and require reopening of the export transaction records. Where export evidence is insufficient or falsified, penalties include: (a) reassessment of the supply at 5% GST/HST, plus interest from the date the return was due; (b) civil penalties under section 285 of the Excise Tax Act for false statements or omissions, up to 25% of the tax sought to be evaded or, in the case of fraudulent claims, 50% of the erroneously claimed refund/credit, plus a separate penalty of up to CAD 500 per false invoice; (c) discretionary penalties and suspension or revocation of GST/HST registration where the person knowingly misrepresents exports; (d) criminal prosecution under the Excise Tax Act or Criminal Code with fines up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment for up to five years; (e) for input tax credit clawbacks, the recipient must repay the full amount credited, with interest, and may be barred from future credit claims. Exporters should maintain contemporaneous evidence of legal export (CBSA export declaration, boll of lading, freight forwarding documents, bank remittance) and a written internal export policy to mitigate scrutiny.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (BOC) - primary central bank; FINTRAC (Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada) - AML/CFT reporting; Minister of Finance (Canada) - exchange control policy oversight; Alberta Treasury Board and Finance - provincial financial regulation of non-depository entities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility for current and capital account purposes. No restrictions on repatriation of profits or capital contributions. However, Canadian financial institutions must apply the Canadian Dollar Large Transaction Reporting to FINTRAC for all FX conversions equal to or greater than CAD 10,000 within 24 hours, and maintain detailed records for fund transfers. The limited partnership may maintain foreign currency bank accounts in CAD and USD without limitation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender requirement. Export proceeds can be retained in any currency. For trade receipts above CAD 10,000, the bank is required to report the transaction to FINTRAC and may require a completed FINTRAC Large Cash Transaction Report (LCTR) or a thorough record of the trade invoice.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with Business Deposit Package
Capital Escrow Account segregated for partner contributions

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: ATB Financial (Alberta Treasury Branches, since 2017 - ATB Financial)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate feasibility for offshore digital Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) such as Wise Business, Payoneer, and Mercury. Canadian regulators do not certify foreign EMIs as banking institutions. Foreign EMIs cannot qualify for Canadian Deposit Insurance (CDIC). For a limited partnership with Alberta nexus, using a foreign EMI for inbound capital injections is legally permissible but may be delayed by compliance reviews and may not provide the required Canadian debits for provincial GST/HST registration. For cross-border trade settlements and treasury clearing, a Canadian domestic bank account remains mandatory to issue Commercial Letters of Credit (LCs). Offshore EMIs are viable only as supplemental receiving rails for PayPal and Stripe payouts, and must be linked to the Canadian corporate bank account for final settlement. The partner must recognize that foreign EMI processing entities may charge additional FX spreads.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Most Tier-1 Canadian banks allow remote onboarding via video interview (e.g., RBC, TD, BMO). A physical presence is not mandatory for a Canadian-established limited partnership if all partners are non-resident. The bank may require an in-person verification of the partnership's registered agent or general partner if opening in a physical branch. Remote opening is generally permitted for accounts that do not involve high-risk jurisdictions, but the bank will require: (a) the limited partnership's certificate of registration from Alberta Corporate Registry, (b) the complete partnership agreement with signatures, (c) the business number (BN) from the CRA, (d) proof of identity and address for each partner with 25% or more interest, (e) a copy of the general partner's certificate of existence (if a corporation), and (f) a resolution from the general partner authorizing the account opening. A video conference with the Account Manager is often used to verify identity, but the bank may require an in-person appointment for the initial sign-off in a regional branch if the risk profile is elevated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident partners with a high-risk jurisdiction passport or address (e.g., FATF grey-list countries)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a detailed OECD-CRS compliance declaration, tax identification numbers, a source-of-wealth statement (including financial statements of the partners' affiliated companies), and a professional legal opinion from a Canadian counsel that the LP is carrying on a legitimate tabletop gaming goods manufacturing business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large initial capital injection (e.g., USD 250,000) without a prior long-term credit relationship
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the executed limited partnership agreement showing capital commitments, the notarized certificate of incorporation of the general partner, a certified copy of the partners' bank statements for the last 12 months, and a business plan with pro forma cash-flow projections for the RPG dice production and sales.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent business purpose code or unclear transaction narrative (e.g., 'merchandise purchase' vs 'capital contribution')
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Use a standardized SWIFT purpose code (e.g., 'Capital Contribution - Equity Injection' for inbound capital and 'Trade Settlement - Goods' for outbound payments). Provide the relevant invoices, bills of lading, and customs entry records from the Canada Border Services Agency to substantiate the commercial nature.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency payouts from PayPal and Stripe in small amounts, which may appear like cash structuring to AML systems
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a monthly reconciliation report showing the match between processed sales orders and bank deposits. Provide a copy of the merchant service provider agreement (PayPal/Stripe) with the LP's name and a description of the automated payout schedule (daily/weekly).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of a third-party intermediary (EMI) for a first cross-border transfer from outside Canada
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the EMI's KYC-completed account statement, the source-of-funds declaration for the originating account, and an attorney's letter from the originating bank confirming sender's identity and FATCA/CRS status. Attach the underlying Kickstarter funding receipt and reconciliation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols: (a) Draw the wire from a foreign bank account in the partner's legal name to the LP's Canadian bank account using an MT103 (SWIFT) or equivalent. (b) The wire transfer instruction MUST include: the partnership's registered business number (BN) or account number, the name of the recipient as 'ABC Limited Partnership - (Alberta)', and the purpose code 'NGIC' (Non-government Investment Capital) or 'CONS' (Consumption) depending on the remitting bank's coding system. For payments from the US, the remitter should use a Federal Reserve Wire (Fedwire) or the Clearing House Interbank Payments System (CHIPS) if the Canadian bank has a USD correspondent. (c) Where the initial capital exceeds CAD 50,000, the bank may require a signed 'Inbound Capital Declaration' form from the LP stating the funds are not proceeds of crime and will be used for legitimate business development. (d) The bank must verify the transfer against the partnership agreement's capital contribution schedule. If the LP receives foreign capital from a partner, the transfer is not subject to any exchange control approval; however, if the capital is provided in-kind (epoxy resin machinery, molds), the LP must apply to the Alberta Corporate Registry to update the Statement of Creditor and Partner Information. (e) For payment routing through the Bank of Canada's Large Value Transfer System (LVTS), the Canadian bank may pre-clear the incoming transfer if it exceeds CAD 10 million; such threshold is not relevant here. (f) The LP should retain the SWIFT confirmation (MT103) and any accompanying payment confirmation from the remitter's bank for 6 years for CRA purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: (1) SWIFT MT103 direct wire transfers - suitable for supplier payments for raw materials (epoxy resin, pigments, silicone molds) up to USD 50,000 per transaction. The LP must include the invoice number and the supplier's bank details; the Canadian bank will use the Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication network to send a full-recourse MT103 to the beneficiary's bank. (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) - recommended for large-repeat purchases from a foreign supplier (e.g., China or India) where the LP has no established trade credit. The LP opens an irrevocable sight LC with its Canadian bank, naming the supplier as beneficiary. The LC is advised and possibly confirmed by the supplier's local bank. The LC must cover the goods' value, freight, and insurance. The FP uses Incoterms 2020 (e.g., EXW, FOB, CIF) to allocate costs. The beneficiary's invoice, packing list, and shipping documents must be presented through the bank's documentary collection channel. (3) PayPal Merchant Account with a cross-border withdrawal to the Canadian bank account - a (USD/CAD) settlement via Automated Clearing House (ACH or EFT) or a SWIFT USD wire. For PayPal payouts, the settlement is in a bundled transfer; the LP should not use PayPal for international trade with non-registered suppliers as it may be restricted. (4) Stripe payouts to the bank account (for Kickstarter and direct web sales) - Stripe sends a settlement via local ACH (Canadian Direct Settlement) in CAD if the LP's bank is CDIC-insured. For US dollar sales, Stripe can either convert to CAD at its spread or hold USD in a Stripe Treasury account, which is not recommended under OFSI's consumer-facing rules. (5) For disbursements to a foreign supplier, the LP must ensure the payment instruction includes the supplier's IBAN and BIC/SWIFT code, and the regulatory format should comply with the Payment Services Directive (PSD2) if receiving display for EU suppliers. The LP may also utilize a Commercial 'Bank Payment Obligation' if the supplier's bank subscribes to the SWIFT Trade Services Utility, but that structure is not required for this scope.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward foreign exchange contracts (plain vanilla FX forwards) for USD/CAD and EUR/CAD - permitted for commercial hedging of payment/collection exposure up to 12 months tenor with a Canadian Schedule I bank or a registered Canadian securities dealer

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies of emerging market suppliers (e.g., CNY, INR) - only permissible if the counterparty is a Schedule II bank or a registered foreign bank branch, and the NDF is used for legitimate commercial trade risk mitigation; NDFs for CAD/USD are non-standard and rarely available in Canada due to full convertibility

Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps) - allowed for Canadian limited partnerships provided the swap is entered into for hedging of actual or anticipated commercial cash flows and is not a speculative financial instrument (the income inclusion for tax purposes under section 92.1 of the Income Tax Act is not triggered if the LP is not 'trading or dealing in derivatives')
Currency options on major traded pairs (USD/CAD, EUR/CAD) - permissible through a qualified over-the-counter dealer; must be cleared through central counterparty under OSFI's SFT rules
Physical settlement of forward trades using the same-day LVTS payment - allowed and recommended, to avoid any mark-to-market issues

Permissible structured commodity-linked forwards if they settle only in CAD and are used for the physical purchase of resin materials - subject to suitability review by the LP's investment advisor and a hedge effectiveness assessment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Registrar of Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each registration anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD$100; continued non-compliance may trigger administrative cancellation of the limited partnership registration by the Registrar.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after the partnership fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties under the Income Tax Act for failing to file an information return, plus possible judicial enforcement; repeat default may jeopardize the limited partnership's standing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory independent audit applies to an Alberta limited partnership under the Partnership Act; an audit obligation may arise solely from the partnership agreement, lender covenants, or the general partner's contractual undertakings.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or ASPE depending on the limited partnership's financial reporting policy; for income tax purposes, partnership income must be computed on a consistent basis in accordance with the Income Tax Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta does not impose a standalone UBO annual confirmation on limited partnerships. The general partner must keep current the identity of limited partners and capital contributions; any change in general partner or limited partner details must be reflected in the LP annual return and, where required, updated with the Alberta Corporate Registry.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Alberta Limited Partnership is a flow-through entity, so no entity-level corporate tax applies. Canadian-resident corporate partners reporting their allocable LP income may benefit from the federal general Part I rate of 15% plus Alberta corporate rate of 8%, for a combined 23%. Eligible Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) partners may apply the federal small business rate (9%) and Alberta small business rate (4%) on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income, subject to income allocation and business limit rules. Alberta does not provide general corporate tax holidays. Qualifying manufacturing and processing profits may be eligible for the federal M&P deduction where the corporate partner meets the statutory activity tests.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 Partnership Information Return; filed electronically through CRA-approved tax software or CRA XML/EFILE channels
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; one return per partnership fiscal year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing is due no later than 5 months after the LP's fiscal year-end, e.g., 31 May for a 31 December year-end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 9-digit BN assigned by the CRA for the Alberta LP, including the applicable program account codes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the LP's BN; non-resident partners do not supply their own BN on this form.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from the handmade sharp-edge epoxy resin liquid core RPG dice business, including Kickstarter, Stripe, and PayPal sales, before deducting expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all sales attributable to the Canadian commercial activity; foreign-source business income of non-resident partners should not be commingled with the LP's Canadian income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Eligible expenses including resin and mould raw materials, sharp-edge tumbling/polishing costs, packaging, shipping, platform processing fees, and arm's-length subcontract labour
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners may only claim deductions for expenses incurred for the purpose of the Canadian LP; overseas home-office or personal expenses must be excluded and supported by contemporaneous records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 200 - Net income (loss) of the partnership
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocable partnership income or loss before partner-specific tax adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must use this allocated amount to file a Canadian Part I tax return (T1 for individuals, T2 for corporations, T3 for trusts) and may claim applicable DTA relief to prevent double taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box I - Limited partners' share schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of partnership income, losses, and other amounts to each limited partner, including percentage ownership changes during the year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident limited partners must be separately identified; distributions of current-year income are not remitted as dividends but are subject to Part I tax in the hands of the non-resident partner.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of CAD 10 per day, to a maximum of CAD 5,000. If the failure is made knowingly or with gross negligence, the CRA may impose a separate penalty of up to 50% of the evaded tax. Continuing non-filing may also invalidate loss allocations claimed by partners and trigger audit expansion.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return; filed via CRA-approved EFILE software or paper where applicable
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly tax instalments when the corporation's annual tax instalment threshold (CAD 3,000) is exceeded
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due 6 months after the corporation's taxation year-end, e.g., 30 June for a calendar-year taxpayer

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate partner's allocable share of the Alberta LP's business income as reported on T5013, plus any other Canadian-source income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporate partner reports only Canadian-source income, including the LP allocation. Foreign-source business income of the non-resident partner is outside the T2 return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal tax at 15% plus Alberta tax at 8% on the corporate partner's taxable income derived through the Alberta LP
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporate partner's active business income allocated through the LP is taxed under Part I on a net basis, subject to treaty protection. Withholding under Part XIII may apply only to specified passive distributions, not to active business allocations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 24 - Net gains on disposition of capital property
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital gains and losses realized by the LP on sharp-edge moulds, workspace equipment, and other capital assets, allocated to corporate partners
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dispositions of taxable Canadian property held through the LP by a non-resident corporate partner must be reported on the T2 return; DTA relief may apply where the property is not connected with a Canadian permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of all non-arm's length transactions with non-residents exceeding CAD 1 million in aggregate value, including related-party dice sales, intellectual property licences, and management fees
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident controlling partners and related distributors must be disclosed; contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation must be prepared and kept to support arm's-length amounts on Form T106.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late T2 filing penalty is 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month, up to 12 months. A second and subsequent failure within a three-year window attracts 10% plus 2% per full month to 24 months. Gross negligence penalties may be 50% of the understated tax. Unpaid tax bears interest compounded daily at prescribed rates.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke reduced DTA withholding on dividends and other periodic payments from an Alberta LP or its corporate partners, the non-resident recipient must provide a valid Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by the home tax authority and complete CRA Form NR301, Declaration of Entitlement to Treaty Benefits. The payer must assess whether the LOB clause is satisfied, apply the treaty rate (for example, 5% or 15% dividends under the Canada-US DTA, depending on shareholding), and file Form NR4 with the CRA. Treaty benefits must be substantiated before payment; retroactive refunds require an NR7 application within the statutory limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on cross-border royalties and interest is 25% under Part XIII in the absence of a tax treaty. Treaty rates commonly reduce royalties to 0% or 10% (e.g., Canada-US DTA: 10% for industrial/commercial IP royalties, 0% for certain cultural copyright payments) and interest to 0% for arm's-length lenders or 10% for non-arm's length lenders. Payments for embedded IP in resin composites, trademark licensing of a dice brand, or intercompany debt in the LP financing structure must be documented and separately withheld.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 aggregate annual transaction value with non-arm's length non-residents triggers mandatory contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation and T106 filing. A CAD 50,000,000 global group revenue threshold triggers preparation of a Master File. Even below these thresholds, CRA may demand documentation under s.247(9), and penalty protection requires complete, contemporaneous, and defensible transfer pricing records.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not maintain a separate Economic Substance Regulation, but the federal General Anti-Avoidance Rule (s.245 ITA) and the Limitation on Benefits provisions in modern Canada DTAs will strike down arrangements lacking genuine commercial purpose. An Alberta LP that is only a shell, has no physical resin-moulding or dice-polishing premises, employs no staff, and merely contracts or re-invoices through a non-resident affiliate carries fatal economic substance risk. The LP must demonstrate real business activity, physical presence, operational employees, and substantive board decisions in Alberta.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully omitting Kickstarter, Stripe, or PayPal gross revenues; fabricating raw-material invoices; destroying point-of-sale or crowdfunding records; or maintaining a dual set of books to understate dice-sale income allocated to the Canadian LP
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Income Tax Act (s.238 and s.239), conviction for tax evasion by means of false statements or omissions carries a fine ranging from 50% to 200% of the federal and provincial tax evaded, and imprisonment up to 5 years on indictment. Civil reassessment may add arrears interest, gross negligence penalties of 50% on the understated tax, and a prohibition from claiming credit for provincial taxes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers of a corporate general partner are jointly and severally liable for unpaid source withholdings, corporate tax remittances, and penalties under s.227.1 of the Income Tax Act. Personal liability includes civil restitution of the evaded tax, travel bans on departing directors, asset tracing through equitable recovery, and imprisonment upon conviction. A limited partner who participates in management or directs the concealment may be stripped of limited liability under Alberta partnership statutes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the Alberta LP as a bare legal titleholder with no dice-casting equipment, no epoxy-resin inventory, no employees, no Alberta office, no board decisions, and no independent economic risk, used merely to re-invoice sales from a Canadian marketplace into a low-tax jurisdiction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may invoke GAAR under s.245 ITA to deny the avoidance transaction and reallocate income to the controlling non-resident or corporate partner. Transfer pricing reassessment under s.247(2) may be imposed at an arm's-length consideration, with a penalty of 10% of the net adjustment where documentary obligations are not met. Treaty relief may be denied under the LOB provision, resulting in a full 25% Part XIII withholding on deemed distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the corporate general partner may be assessed personally for gross negligence penalties and reinstated tax liabilities. Canadian courts will pierce the limited-partnership veil if the limited partner exercises control over the LP's daily commercial activity, creating unlimited personal liability. Directors face civil actions by the CRA for restitution and, where accomplices to the sham arrangement, may be made subject to criminal fines and travel bans pending trial.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the LP to collect large crowdfunding and card-not-present Stripe/PayPal payments without conducting know-your-customer verification on limited partners or beneficiary owners; commingling third-party funds with personal accounts; structuring deposits to the LP's bank account to avoid reporting thresholds; or using the dice trade as a conduit for laundering illicit funds
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violations of the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act attract administrative monetary penalties of up to CAD 1,000,000 for non-registered money service businesses and fines for individual officers of up to CAD 500,000. Intentional money laundering may constitute an indictable offence under the Criminal Code, with imprisonment up to 10 years; prohibited economic sanctions can also expose the LP to consolidated penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the general partner are personally liable for AML compliance failures under the PCMLTFA. Personal liability may include restitution orders, seizure of personal assets, travel bans to restrict flight, and imprisonment for money laundering or failure to comply with a disclosure order. Compliant entities maintain full KYC file profiles for every non-resident limited partner and ongoing transaction monitoring for all crowdfunding rails.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling handmade dice to a related non-resident distributor below arm's-length price; paying an excessive management fee to a non-resident affiliate; failing to charge interest on intercompany shareholder loans; or distributing profits to non-resident limited partners without paying Part XIII withholding on deemed taxable payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under s.247 ITA, CRA may adjust the taxpayer's revenue and expenses to fair arm's-length values. A penalty equal to 10% of the net transfer pricing adjustment is imposed where the documented sale was a gross overstatement or understatement and records were not prepared. Failure to withhold Part XIII tax on royalties or interest results in a payer liability of 100% of the withheld amount, plus interest and penalties. Late or inaccurate Form T106 filings carry separate penalties of CAD 1,000 per month up to CAD 24,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the corporate general partner are jointly and severally liable for unremitted Part XIII withholding under s.227.1. The CRA may personally collect from the director, place liens on personal homes, and pursue director's civil certificates for the unpaid amount. Transfer pricing fraud with fraudulent materials or steps may be prosecuted criminally, exposing the director to fines, travel restrictions, and imprisonment up to 5 years.
